summary: The design addresses the main coupling, but several contracts are underspecified where the existing implementation is strongly database- and BotManager-oriented. The highest risks are asynchronous target resolution, uniform CRUD semantics across three backends, distributed run-state transitions, and exposing arbitrary service methods.

suggestions.title: Make target resolution explicitly asynchronous and define registry ownership
suggestions.rationale: The proposed synchronous `resolve()` contract cannot represent the existing async `BotManager.get_crew()` and `AgentRegistry.get_instance()` APIs. The repository also has no `TargetRegistry` or `register_target()` implementation; agentd currently supplies a `SingleAgentManager` workaround. Define an async resolver contract and make the service registry manager-scoped or otherwise explicitly lifecycle-bound.

suggestions.title: Specify CRUD semantics separately for db, redis, and code jobs
suggestions.rationale: Current `get_schedule`, `pause_schedule`, `update_schedule`, `delete_schedule`, `run_schedule_now`, and `get_last_result` all assume a Postgres `AgentSchedule` row. Code jobs are only a list fallback, while `run_schedule_now` always creates a DB-backed trampoline. A Redis-only or code job therefore cannot satisfy the claimed uniform API without a separate job-definition abstraction and explicit behavior for missing persistence.

suggestions.title: Namespace coordinator keys as well as Redis jobstore keys
suggestions.rationale: The current Redis jobstore uses global `apscheduler.jobs` and `apscheduler.run_times`, while fire coordination uses a shared `parrot:scheduler:fire:{job_id}:...` key. Code jobs currently use IDs such as `auto_bot_tick`, so two managers can collide even if their jobstore keys are namespaced. Include `registered_name` in coordination keys, keep the default manager name stable for restart compatibility, and provide a single adapter for direct Redis consumers such as `ReminderToolkit`.

suggestions.title: Implement failure counting as an atomic state machine
suggestions.rationale: The proposed shared `consecutive_failures` counter is vulnerable to lost updates if multiple workers read and write state concurrently. The existing completion path performs ordinary row reads and updates, and Redis coordination already makes multi-worker execution a normal case. Define atomic Postgres and Redis transitions for success, `target_missing`, `error`, reset, threshold crossing, disable, and alert deduplication; do not let a missing-target `SKIPPED` result look like a successful APScheduler execution.

suggestions.title: Restrict callable methods for service targets
suggestions.rationale: The current execution path uses `getattr(agent, method_name)` and invokes any callable method named by the request. Generalizing this to arbitrary registered service objects expands the attack surface substantially. Require registration-time method allowlists or callable wrappers, reject private and dunder names, and ensure the HTTP/RPC authorization layer is applied before resolving or invoking a service target.

suggestions.title: Define the auto-disable alert destination and delivery contract
suggestions.rationale: `NotificationMixin.send_notification()` requires recipients, but the proposed auto-disable policy specifies neither recipients nor provider configuration. The existing `_SchedulerNotification` helper is only used for configured result emails. Add an explicit per-schedule or global alert configuration, define failure handling when notification delivery fails, and make alerts idempotent across workers.

suggestions.title: Freeze the run-state schema and timezone conversion rules before splitting code
suggestions.rationale: The current model and update path use naive `datetime.now()` values despite timezone-aware database columns, and all run state currently lives in `metadata`. The new model needs explicit types and serialization for `last_result`, delivery outcomes, and `consecutive_failures`, plus a single UTC-aware conversion rule for model defaults, writes, APScheduler events, and API responses.

suggestions.title: Validate Redis job definitions as versioned, data-only payloads
suggestions.rationale: `RedisJobStore` persists jobs through pickle, while the existing implementation deliberately keeps DB trampoline kwargs string-only and stores process-local callbacks separately. Redis backend definitions must reject live callables, service objects, non-JSON metadata, and secrets; use a versioned definition envelope so code changes can detect incompatible persisted jobs instead of failing during APScheduler unpickling.

suggestions.title: Give code jobs a first-class record instead of inferring metadata from job names
suggestions.rationale: Current code jobs capture bound methods in `_auto_tasks`, serialize only a partial synthetic payload, and derive `agent_name` and `method_name` by partitioning `job.name`. Generalized object scanning and names containing dots will make that inference brittle. Store a structured process-local code-job record keyed by APScheduler ID and define exact pause, update, delete, run-now, and last-result behavior for it.

suggestions.title: Resolve the duplicate legacy HTTP surface during the hard cut
suggestions.rationale: The repository currently has the mounted `/api/v1/parrot/scheduler/schedules` handler plus an older `SchedulerHandler` embedded in `manager.py`, both using `agent_name`-era fields. The accepted design names `/api/v1/scheduler/jobs`, which is not the current route. Choose one canonical route, migrate or deliberately alias the old route, remove stale handler code, and convert positional internal callers such as saved-execution scheduling to explicit `target_kind` and `target_name` arguments.

suggestions.title: Add tenant and authorization semantics before exposing service schedules
suggestions.rationale: The current schedule model stores `created_by` and `created_email` but has no tenant scope, and the scheduler handler lists and mutates schedules through a shared manager. A generic service target makes cross-tenant invocation materially more dangerous. Define ownership fields and enforce scope on list, read, update, pause, delete, and run-now rather than treating creator metadata as authorization.

suggestions.title: Build a backend-parity and restart test matrix before the extraction
suggestions.rationale: Existing tests are centered on `AgentSchedule`, the DB trampoline, and headless startup; they do not establish Redis-only restart, code-job CRUD, async resolver behavior, atomic failure thresholds, or timezone-aware state. Add contract tests using fake DB/Redis/memory stores that exercise the same operations and result payloads for all three backends, plus a two-manager collision and three-failure scenario.
